stories.title: Any terror attack originating from Pakistan will invite stronger response: Rajnath Singh
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 15: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh on Thursday said any terrorist act originating from Pakistan would invite an even stronger response from India, asserting that Operation Sindoor, the Balakot airstrikes and surgical strikes marked a shift from diplomatic condemnation to proactive action against terrorism. Addressing a Defence Conclave in New Delhi, Singh said India remained committed to peace but its commitment should not be mistaken for weakness. “Our commitment to peace remains steadfast, yet we are fully prepared to confront any challenge,” he said, adding that India was determined to safeguard its sovereignty, territorial integrity and national interests. Singh said the three military operations symbolised India's approach of targeting the sources of terrorism rather than limiting its response to diplomatic condemnation. He also claimed that since 2014, the “shelf life” of most terrorists had fallen to less than a year, with security forces neutralising them within a year of taking up arms against India. Highlighting the changing security landscape, the Defence Minister warned of emerging threats, including lone-wolf attacks and what he described as “white-collar terrorism”. He said terrorism was evolving beyond organised groups, making it increasingly difficult for security agencies to identify radicalised individuals and prevent potential attacks. Singh also referred to the recent incident involving a co-pilot who allegedly attempted to crash a passenger aircraft and Indian Captain Smit Machchhar, who risked his life to avert a major disaster. He said the incident highlighted the threat posed by lone-wolf attackers and underscored the importance of alert and responsible citizens in preventing terrorist plots. “The fight against terrorism requires not only the capabilities of security agencies but also the active participation of aware and responsible citizens,” he said. Singh described the emerging security environment as one characterised by hybrid, high-tech and hyper warfare. He identified what he termed the “5D Security Threat” — disinformation, destabilisation, disruption, deception and destruction — and called for greater vigilance and preparedness. On defence preparedness, the minister called for a “smart power” approach that combines advanced weaponry, artificial intelligence, human intelligence and cost-effective technologies to address evolving security challenges. He said India needed to integrate precision-guided weapons and loitering munitions with affordable, agile and adaptable systems to strengthen its defence capabilities. Singh attributed India's growing defence capabilities to reforms undertaken under Prime Minister Narendra Modi, saying the government had shifted its focus from meeting immediate military requirements to building a self-reliant and future-ready defence ecosystem. He said defence production had increased to a record level of over Rs 1.78 lakh crore from around Rs 40,000 crore in 2014, while defence exports had risen to an all-time high of Rs 39,000 crore from Rs 686 crore in 2013-14. Indian defence products, he said, were now reaching nearly 100 countries. The minister expressed confidence that India would achieve defence production worth Rs 2 lakh crore in the current year and Rs 3 lakh crore by 2029, while targeting defence exports worth Rs 50,000 crore by the same year. Emphasising domestic manufacturing, Singh said more than 500 companies were engaged in the defence sector, while over 16,000 micro, small and medium enterprises were contributing to the country's defence industrial ecosystem. He said the government had earmarked 75 per cent of the defence modernisation budget for procurement from Indian industries and highlighted initiatives to promote indigenous defence equipment and technology. Singh also highlighted the role of start-ups and young innovators in developing drones, artificial intelligence, quantum technology, cybersecurity and robotics. He said the Ministry of Defence had approved procurement of goods and services worth over Rs 2,400 crore from start-ups and MSMEs and sanctioned projects worth more than Rs 1,500 crore for developing new technologies. The minister said India was steadily progressing towards self-reliance in defence manufacturing, with 159 of the 175 ammunition variants used by the armed forces now being produced domestically. Singh concluded by expressing confidence that India would emerge as a developed nation by the centenary of its independence and provide global leadership in technology, the economy and defence.

He emphasised that while India’s cultural ethos favoured dialogue, coexistence and peaceful resolution of disputes, its commitment to peace should not be mistaken for weakness.

“Operation Sindoor, Balakot Airstrikes and Surgical Strikes weren’t just military operations; they symbolised a decisive shift in the nation’s approach, moving from diplomatic condemnation to proactive action aimed at rooting out terrorism by reaching its very source,” Singh said at the Times Network Defence Conclave in New Delhi.

Defence Minister termed strength and capability as essential to maintaining peace, and underlined that India hopes for peace, but remains prepared for war that sometimes becomes necessary to protect the nation.
“Our commitment to peace remains steadfast, yet we are fully prepared to confront any challenge.

Our goal is to build an India that, while advocating for peace, remains vigilant when it comes to security and is fully capable of safeguarding its sovereignty, integrity, and national interests,” he said.
On the evolving security landscape, Singh underscored the need for heightened vigilance and preparedness in an era of hybrid, high-tech and hyper warfare.

He highlighted the growing complexity of security threats in the digital age, identifying what he described as the ‘5D Security Threat ’-Disinformation, Destabilisation, Disruption, Deception and Destruction.

He pointed out that terrorism was evolving beyond organised groups, and emerging threats include ‘lone-wolf’ attacks and ‘white-collar terrorism’, which make it increasingly difficult for security agencies to identify radicalised individuals and prevent potential attacks.

The Defence Minister referred to the recent incident involving a co-pilot who allegedly attempted to crash a passenger aircraft and Captain Smit Machhar who risked his life to avert a major terror attack.
“The incident underscored the threat posed by lone-wolf attackers while demonstrating how the courage and commitment of an individual could thwart the designs of those driven by hatred.
A single alert and courageous individual could help foil an entire terrorist plot.
On defence preparedness, Singh underscored the need to combine ‘hard power’ with ‘soft power’ and called for a shift towards ‘smart power’.

“Modern defence strategies must integrate precision-guided weapons and loitering munitions with cost-effective weaponry, human intelligence with artificial intelligence, and advanced systems with low-cost, agile and adaptable technologies to address evolving security challenges,” he said.

On the growth witnessed by the defence sector due to the Government’s efforts, Singh stated that defence production has risen to a record over Rs 1.78 lakh crore from Rs 40,000 crore in 2014, with defence exports touching an all-time high of Rs 39,000 crore from Rs 686 crore in 2013-14, and India defence products reaching nearly 100 countries.

He exuded confidence that the nation would achieve defence production targets of Rs 2 lakh crore this year and Rs 3 lakh crore by 2029, and export defence equipment worth Rs 50,000 crore by 2029, the Ministry said in its statement.

The Defence Minister attributed the growth to reforms that simplified export procedures, including the introduction of the Defence EXIM Portal, online approvals, the Open General Export License, streamlined quality certification and the ‘Green Channel’ policy.
These measures, he said, enhanced India’s global credibility and prepared domestic industries to compete in international markets.

"The Ministry of Defence has approved procurement of goods and services worth over Rs 2,400 crore from start-ups and MSMEs and sanctioned projects exceeding Rs 1,500 crore for new technology development.
As of March 2026, iDEX had engaged 676 start-ups and innovators and facilitated the signing of 551 contracts.

From a few dozen defence startups in 2018, the ecosystem had grown to more than 2,000, with young enterprises working across drones, artificial intelligence, quantum technology, cybersecurity, robotics and other advanced fields,” he added.

Citing progress in ammunition manufacturing, he said 159 of the 175 ammunition variants used by the Defence Forces were now indigenously produced, representing more than 90 per cent self-reliance in ammunition variants.

Referring to India’s exports of bulletproof jackets to over 100 countries, he noted that the country was the fourth in the world to establish a national standard for bulletproof jackets aligned with international norms.
He also spoke about the implementation of the One Rank.
One Pension scheme and the creation of the Chief of Defence Staff post, terming them significant measures undertaken to strengthen the defence framework.

article_sentences: The story so far: From Sukumar Sen's tenure, during which the first general election in India was held in 1951-52, to October 16, 1986, the Election Commission had only one member: the Chief Election Commissioner.
In S.S. Dhanoa.

Union of India (1991), the Supreme Court stressed that under Article 342(2) of the Constitution, the President could fix and appoint as many Election Commissioners as he may, from time to time, determine, though it was desirable to have a multi-member commission.

In October 1989, when the Rajiv Gandhi government was in power, the President notified the appointment of Mr. Dhanoa and V.S. Seigell as Election Commissioners to complete the team with Chief Election Commissioner R.V.S. Peri Sastry.

The premise was the increased workload in conducting the elections after the minimum voting age was lowered from 21 to 18, but political observers then saw it as a move by the government to hem Mr. Sastry in.

The multi-member arrangement was short-lived as the President revoked his 1989 notification after the new V.P. Singh government took over and was not in favour of the appointments made by the previous government.
Mr. Dhanoa went to court, which said it was the President’s discretion to determine the number of Election Commissioners.

In the current situation, when two Election Commissioners, Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, have objected to the style of functioning of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, here is a look at the episodic disputes on the panel that have broken out in public.
On October 1, 1993, the President appointed M.S. Gill and G.V.G. Krishnamurthy as Election Commissioners.
Ever since, the commission has been a three-member body.

The President promulgated an Ordinance, later enacted as the Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners (Condition of Service) Amendment Act, with retrospective effect from October 1, 1993.
The Act explicitly granted coordinate powers to the Election Commissioners, solving a grey area in the Constitution.

stories.headline: US teen held over alleged plot to attack Hindu place of worship
stories.title: US teen held over alleged plot to attack Hindu place of worship
stories.summary: New York, Oct 15 : A teenager was arrested for allegedly plotting to carry out a "mass shooting" at a Hindu place of worship in the US state of Illinois, with investigators recovering a manifesto expressing white supremacist ideology and references to violence against people of Indian descent. Alexandros Paporakis, 19, of Palatine village was arrested on October 11 and charged with making a terrorist threat and unlawful possession of a weapon. According to investigators, the youth had tried to open fire "potentially targeting" the place of worship in the Aurora city in Illinois, but his gun jammed, forcing him to drive back home, a move that prevented a mass murder. The specific intended location has not been disclosed by the authorities. Palatine Police detectives examined electronic communications and a document attributed to Paporakis titled "Why I Fought: A.K.A.: (Aurora Shooter's Manifesto)", which contained "statements expressing white supremacist and extremist ideologies, including references to violence directed toward individuals of South Asian heritage, particularly those of Indian descent". Detectives believe Paporakis may have been planning to carry out the attack on October 11. "However, the specific intended location has not been confirmed and remains under investigation," police said on Wednesday. The Consulate General of India in Chicago said it appreciated the timely action by law enforcement authorities and was in touch with members of the Indian diaspora while closely monitoring developments. The arrest comes amid celebrations of Hindu festivals, including Navaratri and Durga Puja, and just two weeks after the Shree Swaminarayan Vadtal Dham Hindu Mandir in Richmond Heights, Ohio, was vandalised. On October 11, the Palatine Police Department was contacted by the Mount Prospect Police Department regarding information it had received about a potential mass shooting. The information originated from an individual who reported receiving concerning electronic communications from Paporakis. According to a report by NBC Chicago, Paporakis had worked as a cashier at fast-food restaurant Taco Bell and had plotted to carry out a "mass shooting of Indian people" at a Hindu temple in Aurora. He drove to the temple last Sunday "decked out for war". The day he chose to carry out the carnage at the sprawling place of worship was filled with people. He was "one malfunctioning rifle away from becoming a mass shooter". Paporakis showed up "to kill a significant number of Indians", the report said, quoting police. Investigators said he had a "modified AR-style rifle and 300 rounds of ammo, enough to fill ten magazines for reloading, along with body armour, gasoline cans" and an assortment of Hakenkreuz (hooked cross used by Nazis), the report said. Paporakis allegedly drove from his mother's home in Palatine to the Aurora temple. Authorities said that "he tried to open fire but the gun jammed, so he drove home". There he "searched the internet trying to learn how to unjam his gun and called a colleague, informing them of (his) intent to carry out a mass shooting". The co-worker then notified the police, informing them of the plot, and Paporakis was arrested Sunday before he could return to the temple. The youth was arrested as he was leaving his residence following a coordinated response by the Palatine and Mount Prospect police departments. Paporakis has been charged with one count of making a terrorist threat and one count of unlawful possession of weapons. He appeared for a detention hearing on Wednesday at the Cook County Third Municipal District Courthouse in Rolling Meadows, where a judge ordered him detained. His next court appearance is scheduled for October 30. According to investigators, Paporakis "expressed pleasure calling himself a sociopathic white supremacist Neo-Nazi filled with hatred, fantasising about mass murder nearly every day". In a social media post, the Hindu American Foundation commended law enforcement for swift action. "We also urge the community to stay vigilant and report any potential threat. Every community deserves to worship without fear," it said. The Coalition of Hindus of North America (CoHNA) said the "disturbing plot" comes as Hindus gather in large numbers to celebrate Navratri, and just two weeks after an attack on a temple in Ohio. "Hindu temples and all houses of worship must be sanctuaries of peace, prayer, and solace - NEVER targets of hate, violence, or terror. We thank law enforcement for their swift action in averting what could have been an unspeakable tragedy. "We urge elected officials and law enforcement agencies to take the growing threats against Hindu places of worship seriously, strengthen protections, and unequivocally condemn Hinduphobia," it said in a social media post. The group called on temples and community organisations to review their security measures, remain vigilant, and promptly report suspicious activity. "The freedom to worship without fear is a fundamental American right. It must be protected," it said. Police said they were working with the FBI as the investigation continued, including a review of possible additional charges. Authorities have not identified any known ongoing threat to the public associated with the incident. "The seriousness of this alleged threat cannot be overstated... Protecting our communities and places of worship remains a priority," Palatine Police Chief William Nord said. FBI Chicago Special Agent in Charge Ryan Whalen said the agency aggressively works alongside its local and state law enforcement partners to identify, investigate, and dismantle any threats of violence driven by radical ideologies. stories.headline: India’s merchandise exports climb 23% to $44.4 bn in September
stories.title: India’s merchandise exports climb 23% to $44.4 bn in September
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 15 : India's merchandise exports recorded a robust 23.04 per cent growth year-on-year to touch a four-month high of $44.4 billion in September this year, despite the uncertainties in global markets and the disruption in shipping due to the escalating Middle East conflict, official figures released on Thursday showed. Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agarwal said the growth trend in India's exports was continuing, indicating sustained momentum in outbound shipments. The growth in goods exports was driven by a broad-based increase in shipments across sectors, with particularly strong growth in petroleum products, meat, dairy and poultry products, handicrafts, and some cereals, he added. Imports rose 8 per cent to $74.61 billion during the month due to the increase in prices of crude oil in the global market. The surge in exports also led to a narrowing of the trade deficit to $30.21 billion during the month on a year-on-year basis from around $33 billion recorded in September 2025. However, on a sequential basis, the trade deficit was higher than the corresponding figure of $26.86 billion in the previous month of August. Cumulatively, goods exports stood at $259.89 billion during April-September, up nearly 19 per cent year-on-year. Imports rose 16 per cent year-on-year to $437.53 billion in the first six months of financial year 2026-27 (FY27). As a result, the merchandise trade deficit stood at $177.64 billion during the six-month period. article_sentences: Principal Secretary to the prime minister, P K Mishra, on Saturday said export restrictions, sanctions and tariffs become instruments of economic policy and they are sometimes even weaponised.
The top government functionary also said that wars disrupt energy and food markets while shipping routes and geographical choke points become sources of economic vulnerability.

Addressing the Kautilya Economic Conclave on the subject 'A World Priced for Risk', he said India is a major energy importer, and any prolonged disruption to an important maritime route can affect the economy adversely.
India's response, therefore, has combined several layers of protection.
"For energy security, the disruption around the Strait of Hormuz has been a particularly clear reminder of how geography can translate into economic risk," he said.
Without mentioning any country, the top official said export restrictions, sanctions and tariffs become instruments of economic policy, sometimes they are even weaponised.
The United States has in the past announced tariffs on a number of countries, including India, for a variety of reasons.

Recently, the US has enacted the 'Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026', which authorises tariffs of up to 100 per cent on nations purchasing Russian oil and gas, including India and China.
Mishra said India has maintained substantial stocks, increased domestic production where possible, diversified procurement, and ensured that alternative supply routes and suppliers are available.
For example, he said, the number of countries from which India imports crude oil has increased from 27 to 43, which is "very large".
"The same logic applies to energy transition.

Greater domestic capacity in renewables, nuclear energy, storage and associated technologies is not only about sustainability, it is also about reducing exposure to external shocks over time," he said.

article_sentences: In a setback to private lender Yes Bank, the Supreme Court on Thursday upheld the Bombay High Court’s judgment quashing the bank’s ₹8,415 crore AT-1 bond write-off.
The verdict has implications for how banks use these instruments to absorb losses during a financial crisis and for investors who hold them.
It could clarify the extent to which banks can write off these instruments during a financial crisis and the legal procedures they must follow.

A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Augustine George Masih delivered its verdict after reserving judgment on 20 May, following submissions from the Centre, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), Yes Bank, bondholders represented by Axis Trustee Services and other investors.
Before reserving judgment, the bench had sought Cabinet records connected with the reconstruction process, including resolutions, meeting minutes and related documents.
It had also sought details of the rules governing the relevant Cabinet meeting, quorum requirements and the names of members present when the decision was taken.
The dispute centres on whether Yes Bank’s administrator had the legal authority to cancel the bonds as part of the bank’s reconstruction plan, leaving investors with losses on their investments.
Additional Tier-1 (AT-1) bonds are financial instruments banks use to raise capital and strengthen their balance sheets.
Introduced under global banking reforms following the 2008 financial crisis, they have no fixed maturity date.
Investors generally receive interest, but the bonds carry higher risks than ordinary debt instruments.
Under specified conditions, they can be written off or converted into shares to absorb losses when a bank faces financial distress.

Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, representing the Centre, the finance ministry, the RBI and Yes Bank, had earlier argued that the write-off was necessary to rebuild the bank’s capital and support its rescue.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court has criticised the manner in which the Allahabad High Court has dealt with a case while granting probation to two men convicted for a brutal attack that left a victim with grievous injuries.
The Court said that the accused were released on probation in ignorance of the adverse report submitted by the probation officer against them.
“The High Court, despite the overwhelming adverse report on the 'character of the offenders' and giving short shrift to the 'nature of the offence', released the accused on good conduct.

There was nothing commending the Court to so release the accused, since the conduct, over the years, of the accused was anything other than 'good'.”, observed a bench of Justice J.B. The High Court upheld the conviction but extended the benefit of Section 4 of the Probation of Offenders Act, 1958 (“PoO Act”), directing the accused to execute personal bonds of ₹20,000 each and maintain peace and good behaviour for one year.
The High Court relied on the passage of approximately 22 years since the incident and the absence of previous convictions.
Aggrieved by the High Court's order, the informant (brother of the victim) moved to the Supreme Court.

stories.title: Supreme Court Quashes Rajasthan High Court's Disciplinary Proceedings Against Judge Over Bail Order
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court has quashed disciplinary proceedings initiated against a Rajasthan judicial officer(since retired) for granting bail to two accused persons despite their earlier bail applications having been rejected by the High Court, observing that counselling or a warning would have sufficed in the peculiar facts of the case.

A bench of Justice B.V. Nagarathna, Justice R. Mahadevan and Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya directed the Rajasthan Government and the High Court to recompute the officer's pay under the revised pay scale and release his terminal benefits, including pension and arrears, within three months, subject to there being no other legal impediment.
The case concerned Mukesh Tyagi, who was serving as a Special Judge under the POCSO Act at Dholpur when he granted bail to two accused persons in May 2019.
The Rajasthan High Court subsequently cancelled the bail, observing that no change in circumstances had occurred after the accused persons' earlier bail applications were rejected.

Following the High Court's direction to place its order before the Chief Justice, disciplinary proceedings were initiated against the petitioner-judicial officer under Rule 16 of the Rajasthan Civil Services (Classification, Control and Appeal) Rules, 1958, alleging gross judicial impropriety and indiscipline, following which the petitioner moved the Supreme Court.
The Supreme Court declined to interfere with the High Court's observations but separately held that the disciplinary inquiry was unwarranted in the circumstances.
“…in the facts and circumstances of this case, the initiation of an inquiry was not at all required.
Possibly the entry of the remarks of the learned Single Judge in the Annual Confidential Report (ACR) would have sufficed.

We have also stated, the petitioner/judicial officer could have been counseled and warned to be more careful in future and to give sufficient weightage to the orders of the High Court particularly when the same were passed earlier in the same case by the High Court.

In the circumstance, we find that the Memorandum dated 25.10.2024 at Annexure P-6, the statement of charges under Rule 16 of the Rules, the allegation of charge etc. were not warranted for in the instant case.”, the Court held.
The Court also noted that the petitioner's Annual Confidential Reports were positive and that he had retired on March 31, 2026, while his revised pay and terminal benefits remained unreleased.
Accordingly, the Court quashed the disciplinary memorandum dated October 25, 2024, and the related charges.

article_sentences: Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar has told the Supreme Court that “preventive measures” taken on October 10 were based on intelligence inputs, ever-changing ground situation, and with an objective of preventing any disturbance of public order.

article_sentences: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday issued notice to the Election Commission of India (ECI), chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and election commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi on a petition filed by Rahul Gandhi and other INDIA bloc leaders alleging large-scale voter deletions and irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and justice Joymalya Bagchi sought responses from the poll panel and the other respondents, and tagged the plea with matters already pending before the court concerning SIR.

The petitioners have sought scrutiny of the ECI’s decision-making during the revision exercise, alleging that decisions were taken without adequate collective deliberation and that eligible voters were excluded without sufficient safeguards.

The plea seeks disclosure of official records, including files, minutes, notings and objections recorded by election commissioners, as well as access logs relating to the ECINET and ERONET electoral-roll databases.

The INDIA bloc leaders have also sought an independent audit of voter deletions, publication of booth-wise lists of deleted electors with reasons for their removal, and an effective mechanism to restore names deleted erroneously.
They have raised concerns over alleged changes to Form 6, which is used to enrol new voters, and sought safeguards against deletion without notice and an opportunity to be heard.

The petition does not seek to reopen the question of whether the ECI has the authority to conduct SIR, but challenges aspects of how the exercise has been implemented and the decisions taken in its course.
During the hearing, the CJI also expressed concern over the conduct of one of the petitioners during the INDIA bloc’s October 12 march to the Supreme Court.
The march, led by Rahul, was organised to protest alleged electoral irregularities and demand Kumar’s resignation.
After lawyers raised objections to the procession, Surya Kant said nobody could “browbeat” the judiciary.
He added, “We are not sitting in an ivory tower, we are aware of things.”
The court clarified that issuing notice on the SIR petition did not amount to condoning the conduct of the political leaders during the march.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court has set aside orders rejecting a claim petition filed by Alladin Charities and Zakat Wakf, which sought to resist the execution of a decree for possession of a property in Hyderabad, and remanded the matter to the executing court for fresh consideration.
A bench of Justices S.V.N. Bhatti and N.V. Anjaria held that the findings recorded by the executing court and the Telangana High Court did not conform to well-established principles of law.
The Court directed the VII Senior Civil Judge, City Civil Court, Hyderabad, to permit both parties to raise fresh pleas, adduce additional evidence and conduct a fresh inquiry in accordance with law.

Wajid Ali and another.

When the decree-holder initiated execution proceedings in 2016 to obtain physical possession, Alladin Charities and Zakat Wakf intervened as a third-party objector, claiming that the property belonged to the trust and was Waqf property.

The trust traced its claim to a Farman Mubarak issued by the then Nizam of Hyderabad, which allegedly conveyed the land to Khan Bahadur Ahmed Alladin Nawab Ahmed Nawaz Jung Bahadur, the founder of the Alladin family trusts, for establishing a Waqf for charitable purposes.
It also relied on historical endowment records, a trust deed executed in 1976 and earlier litigation concerning the property.

stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 15: Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan has tendered an unconditional and unqualified apology to the Supreme Court in a contempt case over alleged violation of the apex court's direction to ensure no “complete prohibition” on Metro and train services in Delhi in the wake of the October 10 protest called by the Cockroach Janta Party. In an affidavit filed in the top court, Mohan said a request was received from Delhi Police to suspend cellular internet services for one day, until 10 pm on October 10. “The request was duly processed and considered in accordance with law and was found to be a proportionate measure, having regard to the magnitude of the situation and the need to prevent any disturbance of public order in the national capital,” Mohan said. The home secretary said that cellular internet services were suspended from 10 pm on October 9 until 10 pm on October 10 within a radius of 4 km of Raisina Hill. He clarified that the suspension was confined to cellular internet services, and did not extend to non-cellular internet services or telecommunication services such as Wi-Fi or broadband. “I state and submit that the suspension of internet services for a limited period and within a defined geographical area, subject to the applicable statutory safeguards, is a recognised measure that may be considered for maintaining public order in appropriate circumstances,” he said. “I therefore respectfully pray that this court may be pleased to modify its order dated October 11 to the extent necessary to permit the suspension of internet services in situations of necessity, strictly in accordance with law and subject to the applicable statutory requirements and safeguards,” he said. A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi is scheduled to hear the matter on Thursday. On October 11, the apex court said that contempt petitioners, who have alleged violations of the court's direction to ensure no complete prohibition on Metro and train services in Delhi due to the protest, have made out a “prima facie” case. The bench had issued notices to Mohan, Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar and Delhi Metro Rail Corporation Chairperson D Thara. The CJP had given the protest call on October 10 to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged electoral irregularities.

stories.headline: "Sonamarg to be developed as year-round tourism destination": CM Omar Abdullah
stories.title: "Sonamarg to be developed as year-round tourism destination": CM Omar Abdullah
stories.summary: Ganderbal, Oct 15 : Chief Minister Omar Abdullah on Thursday said the Jammu and Kashmir government is working on projects to develop Sonamarg as a year-round tourism destination, with plans to promote rafting in summer and skiing, skating and other winter sports during the colder months. “With the construction of the tunnel, Sonamarg is now accessible throughout the year. We want to promote rafting during summer and skiing, skating and other winter sports activities,” Omar told reporters during his visit to Ganderbal, as per the news agency—Kashmir News Observer (KNO). He said he would work with Kangan MLA Mian Mehar Ali to further strengthen Sonamarg’s position on the tourism map. The Chief Minister said forest, environmental and wildlife clearances sometimes caused delays in tourism projects, but maintained that the government would follow all required procedures while developing new tourism destinations. During his visit, he said development projects worth around Rs 60 crore were either inaugurated or had their foundation stones laid in Ganderbal. On the construction of a major bridge over the River Jhelum, estimated to cost Rs 40 crore, he said test piling had been completed and efforts were underway to meet the construction targets. “We are making efforts to complete the pillars by April and the entire bridge by December next year,” he said. The Chief Minister said several road projects, a new school building and infrastructure works at the Fruit and Vegetable Mandi were also inaugurated. He said traders at the mandi had sought its expansion, construction of a boundary wall and a grade separator. The matter, he said, had been discussed with National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) officials, while other demands had also been noted for necessary action. On the demand for fencing the Power Development Corporation (PDC) canal following repeated incidents involving loss of human lives, Omar said the matter would be taken up with the concerned authorities. “If the decision were within my authority, I would have announced it here. We will raise the public demand with the concerned authorities,” he said. Regarding pending compensation cases related to National Highway projects, Omar said newly appointed Deputy Commissioner Shreya would examine the matter after settling into her responsibilities. On traffic congestion caused by Chinar trees along the Beehama–Kheer Bhawani road, the Chief Minister acknowledged the difficulties faced by commuters and stressed the need for a practical solution. “Development and environmental protection must go hand in hand. We may have to remove some trees and plant eight to ten Chinar trees elsewhere, away from roads,” he said. Referring to the 70th National School Sports event being held at the College of Physical Education in Ganderbal, Omar said students from across the country were participating in Wushu and Taekwondo competitions. Reiterating his stand on land acquisition, the Chief Minister said written agreements signed with affected families would be honoured. “Whatever commitments were made in the signed agreements will be implemented,” he said.—(KNO)
